# Intezer Research

> Malware analysis, threat research and thought leadership from Intezer's Research Team: deep dives on the malware families, campaigns and threat actors we track, plus practical guides to malware analysis and reverse engineering.

This site is published by Intezer's Research Team. Please attribute content to "Intezer Research" and link to the page you used. Many blog posts here are also published on intezer.com/blog, which is their canonical home.

- [Blog](https://research.intezer.com/blog/): 104 technical analyses of malware and threat-actor activity, newest first below
- [Knowledge Base](https://research.intezer.com/docs/): practical guides to malware analysis and reverse engineering
- [Presentations](https://research.intezer.com/videos/): conference talks by the team
- [Topics](https://research.intezer.com/tags/): every post grouped by tag

## Blog

- [When Everything Becomes Open-Source](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2026/11/when-everything-becomes-open-source/): AI agents rebuilt maintainable source code for Slack, Apple’s Finder and the TinyTurla-NG backdoor from binaries alone. Compiled code no longer hides source. (2026-11-10)
- [Rubber Ducky in the Sky](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2026/09/rubber-ducky-in-the-sky/): A one-letter typo in a mouse setup address led to a “privacy browser” hiding a remote-control engine in a Microsoft-signed MSIX, part of a ten-year chain. (2026-09-01)
- [When the Whole Company Adopts AI: What It Does to Your SOC](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2026/08/when-the-whole-company-adopts-ai/): Intezer platform data shows AI-related alerts are a small but fast-growing share of SOC alerts, mostly false alarms that bury the genuine AI exposures. (2026-08-25)
- [Two Trojan Families Trotting in Through Google Search Ads](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2026/07/two-trojan-families/): SilentMare, a downloader, and HollowMare, a browser-hijacking PUA, spread via trojanized PDF and file converter apps promoted through Google search ads. (2026-07-27)
- [When the AI Edits Its Own Trust Boundary: Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in AWS's Agentic IDE](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2026/07/remote-code-execution-kiro/): A remote code execution flaw in Kiro, AWS’s agentic IDE: hidden instructions in a web page make it rewrite its MCP config and run code. AWS has patched it. (2026-07-20)
- [How attackers are gaining access to LLM inference](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2026/06/how-attackers-access-llm-inference/): Five routes attackers use to reach LLM inference without paying: offensive LLMs, crypto payment, free-tier APIs, leaked API keys and exposed LLM servers. (2026-06-03)
- [OrBit (Re)turns: Tracking an Open-Source Linux Rootkit Across Four Years of Forks and Deployments](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2026/05/orbit-returns/): OrBit is a fork of the Medusa open-source LD_PRELOAD rootkit. Samples from 2022 to 2026 show two lineages with rotating keys, credentials and evasion hooks. (2026-05-14)
- [Tracing a Paper Werewolf campaign through AI-generated decoys and Excel XLLs](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2025/12/tracing-a-paper-werewolf-campaign-through-ai-generated-decoys-and-excel-xlls/): An Excel XLL add-in drops EchoGather, a new backdoor, with AI-generated decoys. We link the campaign to Paper Werewolf (GOFFEE) via infrastructure and TTPs. (2025-12-19)
- [Frankenstein Variant of the ToneShell Backdoor Targeting Myanmar](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2025/09/frankenstein-variant-of-the-toneshell-backdoor-targeting-myanmar/): A new variant of Mustang Panda’s ToneShell backdoor targeting Myanmar uses anti-analysis stalling, API hashing and updated GUID creation. Includes new IoCs. (2025-09-10)
- [Threat Bulletin: Fire in the Woods – A New Variant of FireWood](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2025/08/threat-bulletin-firewood/): A new, low-detected variant of FireWood, a Linux backdoor of the Project Wood lineage, keeps its core functions but changes implementation and configuration. (2025-08-13)
- [Emerging Phishing Techniques: New Threats and Attack Vectors](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2025/04/emerging-phishing-techniques-new-threats-and-attack-vectors/): Four phishing techniques that reached inboxes in 2025: Base64 JavaScript in SVG files, URLs in PDF annotations, OneDrive links and MHT files inside OpenXML. (2025-04-23)
- [Threat Bulletin: Weaponized Software Targets Chinese-Speaking Organizations](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2025/01/weaponized-software-targets-chinese/): Trojanized MSI installers aimed at Chinese-speaking organizations use a loader we named PNGPlug to deliver ValleyRAT, in a campaign linked to Silver Fox. (2025-01-16)
- [Babble Babble Babble Babble Babble Babble BabbleLoader](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2024/11/babble-babble-babble-babble-babble-babble-babbleloader/): BabbleLoader uses junk code, metamorphism, runtime API resolution and anti-sandbox checks to evade traditional and AI-based detection while delivering stealers. (2024-11-17)
- [Technical Analysis of a Novel IMEEX Framework](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2024/10/technical-analysis-of-a-novel-imeex-framework/): IMEEX is a custom Windows DLL framework seen targeting Djibouti and Afghanistan, with remote control features and signs of infrastructure reuse with ShadowPad. (2024-10-10)
- [There's Something About CryptBot: Yet Another Silly Stealer (YASS)](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2024/09/cryptbot-yet-another-silly-stealer-yass/): YASS, an infostealer labelled CryptBot but sharing little of its code, arrives via the MustardSandwich downloader and IDATLOADER and can drop NetSupport. (2024-09-10)
- [Dissecting SSLoad Malware: A Comprehensive Technical Analysis](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2024/06/ssload-technical-malware-analysis/): SSLoad’s chain from a phishing MSI to PhantomLoader, hidden in a patched 360 Total Security DLL, and a Rust downloader that reads its C2 from Telegram. (2024-06-10)
- [Operation HamsaUpdate: A Sophisticated Campaign Delivering Wipers Puts Israeli Infrastructure at Risk](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2023/12/stealth-wiper-israeli-infrastructure/): Phishing aimed at Israeli F5 users abused a real BIG-IP flaw to deliver new wipers, Hatef for Windows and Hamsa for Linux, plus the Handala AutoIt loader. (2023-12-20)
- [WildCard: The APT Behind SysJoker Targets Critical Sectors in Israel](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2023/11/wildcard-evolution-of-sysjoker-cyber-threat/): WildCard, the APT behind SysJoker, targets critical sectors in Israel with new variants and the Rust-based RustDown, and has links to Operation ElectricPowder. (2023-11-27)
- [Malware Reverse Engineering – Unraveling the Secrets of Encryption in Malware](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2023/08/unraveling-malware-encryption-secrets/): How malware uses XOR, stream and block ciphers and RSA, and how to spot encryption when reversing: imports, CAPA, RC4, ChaCha20 and AES patterns, debugging. (2023-08-07)
- [CryptoClippy is Evolving to Pilfer Even More Financial Data](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2023/05/cryptoclippy-evolves-to-pilfer-more-financial-data/): CryptoClippy, a clipboard stealer aimed at Portuguese speakers, now targets Brazilian payment services such as PIX and is also delivered via NSIS installers. (2023-05-24)
- [How Hackers Use Binary Padding to Outsmart Sandboxes and Infiltrate Your Systems](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2023/05/how-hackers-use-binary-padding-to-outsmart-sandboxes/): Binary padding inflates PE files with junk data to change hashes and beat sandbox size limits. PufferPhishing pads files that still compress by over 90%. (2023-05-18)
- [Phishing Campaign Targets Chinese Nuclear Energy Industry](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2023/03/phishing-campaign-targets-nuclear-energy-industry/): A phishing campaign against China’s nuclear energy industry delivers Excel and CHM payloads, using tactics and techniques that align with Bitter APT. (2023-03-24)
- [Detection Rules for Lightning Framework (and How to Make Them With Osquery)](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/08/lightning-framework-linux-detection-rules-osquery/): Osquery queries for detecting Lightning Framework on Linux, covering its file artifacts, persistence and rootkits, packaged as a ready-to-use query pack. (2022-08-03)
- [Lightning Framework: New Undetected "Swiss Army Knife" Linux Malware ⚡](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/07/lightning-framework-new-linux-threat/): Lightning Framework is a previously undetected modular Linux malware with a downloader, core module and plugins. It can install rootkits and open SSH. (2022-07-21)
- [OrBit: New Undetected Linux Threat Uses Unique Hijack of Execution Flow](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/07/orbit-new-undetected-linux-threat/): OrBit is an undetected Linux threat that hijacks the dynamic loader to infect every process, hooking functions to hide, steal credentials and give SSH access. (2022-07-06)
- [YTStealer Malware: "YouTube Cookies! Om Nom Nom Nom"](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/06/ytstealer-malware-youtube-cookies/): YTStealer steals only YouTube authentication cookies, using anti-analysis code from the Chacal project. Its build path names YouBot Solutions. (2022-06-29)
- [Symbiote Deep-Dive: Analysis of a New, Nearly-Impossible-to-Detect Linux Threat](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/06/new-linux-threat-symbiote/): Symbiote is a Linux malware loaded into every running process via LD_PRELOAD. It hides files, processes and traffic using BPF hooking and harvests credentials. (2022-06-09)
- [SOC Level Up: Threat Hunting and Detection With Sigma](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/05/threat-hunting-sigma-detection-rules/): How to use Sigma rules for threat hunting and detection, from hunting on behavior rather than indicators to writing Sigma detection rules for Emotet. (2022-05-17)
- [How to Write YARA Rules That Minimize False Positives](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/05/yara-rules-minimize-false-positives/): How code reuse between malicious files can generate YARA rules automatically with fewer false positives, with example rules for Emotet and a WannaCry variant. (2022-05-12)
- [Elephant Framework Delivered in Phishing Attacks Against Ukrainian Organizations](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/04/elephant-malware-targeting-ukrainian-orgs/): Elephant, a Go malware framework that includes GrimPlant and GraphSteel, is delivered by spear phishing from spoofed Ukrainian government email addresses. (2022-04-04)
- [New Conversation Hijacking Campaign Delivering IcedID](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/03/conversation-hijacking-campaign-delivering-icedid/): An IcedID campaign hijacks email threads from compromised Exchange servers and delivers ISO files with LNK and DLL payloads to bypass Mark-of-the-Web. (2022-03-28)
- [SOC Level Up: Introduction to Sigma Rules](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/03/intro-to-sigma-rules/): An introduction to Sigma rules for SOC analysts: what they are, how the metadata, log source and detection sections work, and how to compile them for your SIEM. (2022-03-22)
- [Boost Your SOC Skills: How to Detect Good Apps Gone Bad](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/03/boost-your-soc-skills-how-to-detect-good-apps-gone-bad/): How attackers abuse trusted Windows tools such as PsExec, MSHTA, Squiblydoo and WMI, with real attack examples and detection rules SOC analysts can adapt. (2022-03-01)
- [TeamTNT Cryptomining Explosion 🧨](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/02/teamtnt-cryptomining-explosion/): TeamTNT’s cryptojacking campaigns from October 2019 through 2021, moving from Redis to Docker and Kubernetes, with their tooling, timeline, TTPs and IOCs. (2022-02-18)
- [Radare Plugin is Here for Intezer Community](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/02/radare-plugin-automate-reverse-engineering/): The r2analyze community plugin brings Intezer code genomics into Radare2, so reverse engineers can attribute a sample to a malware family or threat actor. (2022-02-08)
- [3 Ways to Save Incident Response Time](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/01/save-incident-response-time-intezer-analyze/): Three ways to cut incident response time: classify files collected from disk images, analyze memory dumps and scan live endpoints for threats loaded in memory. (2022-01-31)
- [Make your First Malware Honeypot in Under 20 Minutes](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/01/how-to-make-malware-honeypot/): Set up a malware honeypot in the cloud with open-source software in under 20 minutes and analyze the attacks it catches, plus the IoCs our honeypot collected. (2022-01-20)
- [Detection Rules for Sysjoker (and How to Make Them With Osquery)](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/01/detection-rules-for-sysjoker-and-how-to-make-them-with-osquery/): Osquery queries for hunting SysJoker on Linux, macOS and Windows, built from its file artifacts and persistence and packaged as a ready-to-use query pack. (2022-01-14)
- [New SysJoker Backdoor Targets Windows, Linux, and macOS](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2022/01/new-backdoor-sysjoker/): SysJoker is a multi-platform backdoor for Windows, macOS and Linux, found on a Linux web server at an educational institution. Analysis, IoCs and detections. (2022-01-11)
- [All Your Go Binaries are Belong to Us](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/12/all-your-go-binaries-are-belong-to-us/): How to extract hidden metadata from stripped Go binaries using the standard library: build info, dependency versions for vulnerability checks, and source maps. (2021-12-02)
- [New Type of Supply Chain Attack Could Put Popular Admin Tools at Risk](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/11/chainjacking-supply-chain-attack-puts-popular-admin-tools-at-risk/): ChainJacking, found with Checkmarx, abuses GitHub username changes to hijack Go packages fetched from repositories, which could put popular admin tools at risk. (2021-11-16)
- [Conducting Digital Forensics Incident Response (DFIR) on an Infected GitLab Server](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/11/dfir-infected-gitlab-server/): Runtime alerts on a GitLab server exposed Metasploit shellcode and an XMRig miner in a container, likely entering via weak credentials or CVE-2021-22205. (2021-11-04)
- [Exposed Prefect Workflows Could Lead to Disruptive Attacks](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/10/exposed-prefect-workflows-could-lead-to-disruptive-attacks/): Hundreds of misconfigured Prefect workflow servers are exposed online, which could let attackers modify or delete workflows, tasks, agents and execution logs. (2021-10-26)
- [Misconfigured Airflows Leak Thousands of Credentials from Popular Services](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/10/misconfigured-airflows-leak-credentials/): Misconfigured Apache Airflow instances exposed credentials for services such as Slack, PayPal and AWS through variables, connections, logs and config files. (2021-10-04)
- [Teaching Capa New Tricks: Analyzing Capabilities in PE and ELF Files](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/09/analyzing-capabilities-in-pe-and-elf-files/): Intezer extended FireEye’s capa to analyze ELF files and added Linux rules. Pairing extracted capabilities with code reuse helps connect malware families. (2021-09-15)
- [Vermilion Strike: Linux and Windows Re-implementation of Cobalt Strike](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/09/vermilionstrike-reimplementation-cobaltstrike/): Vermilion Strike is an undetected Linux re-implementation of Cobalt Strike Beacon, with matching Windows samples, used against telecom, government and finance. (2021-09-13)
- [How to Detect Cobalt Strike](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/08/cobalt-strike-detect-this-persistent-threat/): Cobalt Strike Beacon arrives via Office macros, supply chain attacks, living off the land and EXE files. How to detect each with static and dynamic analysis. (2021-08-18)
- [Guide to Digital Forensics Incident Response in the Cloud](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/08/guide-to-digital-forensics-incident-response-in-the-cloud/): How cloud incident response differs from on-premises forensics, from evidence collection to CSP limits, and how to prepare for, detect and contain attacks. (2021-08-11)
- [New Attacks on Kubernetes via Misconfigured Argo Workflows](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/07/new-attacks-on-kubernetes-via-misconfigured-argo-workflows/): Misconfigured Argo Workflows instances let attackers run unauthorized code on Kubernetes clusters. We found operators already using them to drop cryptominers. (2021-07-20)
- [Targeted Phishing Attack against Ukrainian Government Expands to Georgia](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/07/targeted-phishing-attack-against-ukrainian-government-expands-to-georgia/): A spear phishing campaign against Ukraine’s government expanded to Georgia with an AutoIt infostealer. Similarities to APT28 suggest a possible Russian link. (2021-07-14)
- [Energy Sector and its Suppliers Targeted in Global Phishing Campaign](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/07/global-phishing-campaign-targets-energy-sector-and-its-suppliers/): Typosquatted and spoofed emails with IMG, ISO or CAB attachments drop Agent Tesla, Formbook and other stealers on energy, oil and gas firms and their suppliers. (2021-07-07)
- [Klingon RAT Holding on for Dear Life](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/06/klingon-rat-holding-on-for-dear-life/): Klingon RAT is a Go remote access trojan with mostly unique code that kills antivirus processes, uses many persistence and UAC bypass methods and TLS C2. (2021-06-17)
- [Wrapping Up a Year of Infamous Bazar Campaigns](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/05/wrapping-up-a-year-of-infamous-bazar-campaigns/): A profile of Bazar, the backdoor attributed to the TrickBot gang and named for its EmerDNS .bazar C2 domains, and four prominent campaigns from its first year. (2021-05-27)
- [Why Relying on the Cloud Provider for Security is Not Enough](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/05/why-relying-on-the-cloud-provider-for-security-is-not-enough/): Cloud Snooper, flaws in security tools, misconfigurations and unauthorized workload access show where the built-in security of AWS, Azure and GCP falls short. (2021-05-20)
- [CVE-2021-27075: Microsoft Azure Vulnerability Allows Privilege Escalation and Leak of Private Data](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/05/cve-2021-27075-microsoft-azure-vulnerability-allows-privilege-escalation-and-leak-of-data/): CVE-2021-27075, a flaw in the Azure VM extension mechanism on Linux, let unprivileged users leak extension private data and, with VMAccess, escalate privileges. (2021-05-11)
- [HabitsRAT Used to Target Linux and Windows Servers](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/04/habitsrat-used-to-target-linux-and-windows-servers/): HabitsRAT, a Go RAT first seen on hacked Microsoft Exchange servers, has an undetected Linux variant and runs only commands signed with the attacker’s key. (2021-04-20)
- [Rocke Group Actively Targeting the Cloud: Wants Your SSH Keys](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/04/rocke-group-actively-targeting-the-cloud-wants-your-ssh-keys/): A new Rocke Group variant spreads via saved SSH keys, weak passwords and Jenkins, Redis and ActiveMQ flaws to run a Monero miner on cloud servers. (2021-04-06)
- [New Linux Backdoor RedXOR Likely Operated by Chinese Nation-State Actor](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/03/new-linux-backdoor-redxor-likely-operated-by-chinese-nation-state-actor/): RedXOR, a Linux backdoor posing as polkit daemon, shares traits with Winnti-linked PWNLNX and XOR.DDOS and is likely operated by a Chinese nation-state actor. (2021-03-10)
- [When Viruses Mutate: Did SunCrypt Ransomware Evolve from QNAPCrypt?](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/03/when-viruses-mutate-did-suncrypt-ransomware-evolve-from-qnapcrypt/): Code reuse links SunCrypt ransomware to QNAPCrypt, used against NAS devices in 2019, while dark web research shows the two are run by different actors. (2021-03-02)
- [A Rare Look Inside a Cryptojacking Campaign and its Profit](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/01/a-rare-look-inside-a-cryptojacking-campaign-and-its-profit/): A Linux cryptojacking campaign enters through exposed Docker API ports and installs a Golang Monero miner. Its wallet dashboards show 95 workers and the profit. (2021-01-13)
- [Operation ElectroRAT: Attacker Creates Fake Companies to Drain Your Crypto Wallets](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2021/01/operation-electrorat-attacker-creates-fake-companies-to-drain-your-crypto-wallets/): ElectroRAT, a new Golang RAT for Windows, Linux and macOS, spreads through trojanized crypto apps promoted by fake companies to drain victims’ wallets. (2021-01-05)
- [Early Bird Catches the Worm: New Golang Worm Drops XMRig Miner on Servers](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/12/new-golang-worm-drops-xmrig-miner-on-servers/): An undetected Golang worm spreads to Windows and Linux servers via weak MySQL, Tomcat and Jenkins passwords and WebLogic CVE-2020-14882 to run XMRig. (2020-12-29)
- [A Zebra in Gopher’s Clothing: Russian APT Uses COVID-19 Lures to Deliver Zebrocy](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/12/russian-apt-uses-covid-19-lures-to-deliver-zebrocy/): Sofacy (APT28) used COVID-19 lures about Sinopharm, delivered in VHD files, to drop the Go version of Zebrocy, linked to Sofacy through shared code. (2020-12-09)
- [Stantinko's Proxy After Your Apache Server](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/11/stantinkos-proxy-after-your-apache-server/): A new version of Stantinko’s Linux proxy trojan masquerades as Apache httpd. We analyze version 2.17 and compare it with version 1.2, documented by ESET. (2020-11-24)
- [A Storm is Brewing: IPStorm Now Has Linux Malware](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/10/a-storm-is-brewing-ipstorm-now-has-linux-malware/): IPStorm, a Golang botnet that hides traffic in the IPFS peer-to-peer network, now has Linux variants adding SSH brute forcing, Steam gaming fraud and ad fraud. (2020-10-01)
- [VB2020 - Advanced Pasta Threat: Mapping Malware Use of Open Source Offensive Security Tools](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/09/advanced-pasta-threat-mapping-malware-use-of-open-source-offensive-security-tools/): VB2020 research mapping threat actor use of open source offensive security tools through code reuse, and how those libraries enable code-based YARA signatures. (2020-09-30)
- [Attackers Abusing Legitimate Cloud Monitoring Tools to Conduct Cyber Attacks](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/09/attackers-abusing-legitimate-cloud-monitoring-tools-to-conduct-cyber-attacks/): TeamTNT installs Weave Scope, a legitimate monitoring tool, on victims’ Docker and Kubernetes hosts to map the environment and run commands without malware. (2020-09-08)
- [Using YARA Rules to Turn Open Source Against Malware](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/09/turning-open-source-against-malware/): Threat actors copy open source offensive security libraries like MemoryModule into malware. We show how to build code-based YARA rules that detect this reuse. (2020-09-03)
- [Watch Your Containers: Doki Infecting Docker Servers in the Cloud](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/07/watch-your-containers-doki-infecting-docker-servers-in-the-cloud/): Doki, an undetected Linux backdoor used by the Ngrok Mining Botnet, infects exposed Docker API servers and generates C&C domains from the Dogecoin blockchain. (2020-07-28)
- [The Evolution of APT15's Codebase 2020](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/05/the-evolution-of-apt15s-codebase-2020/): Ketrum, a new APT15 backdoor family merging features of Ketrican and Okrum, shows the group reworking the same codebase rather than changing tactics. (2020-05-21)
- [Kaiji: New Chinese Linux malware turning to Golang](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/05/kaiji-new-chinese-linux-malware-turning-to-golang/): Kaiji is a custom Golang botnet of Chinese origin that brute-forces root SSH logins on Linux servers and IoT devices to launch DDoS attacks. (2020-05-04)
- [Fantastic payloads and where we find them](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/03/fantastic-payloads-and-where-we-find-them/): Emotet, Dridex, Ursnif and TrickBot packers increasingly load payloads with malformed or missing PE headers to hinder analysis and detection. (2020-03-30)
- [New Iranian Campaign Tailored to US Companies Utilizes an Updated Toolset](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/01/new-iranian-campaign-tailored-to-us-companies-uses-updated-toolset/): APT34 targets Westat employees and the US firms that hire Westat with a malicious survey spreadsheet, dropping undetected TONEDEAF 2.0 and VALUEVAULT 2.0. (2020-01-30)
- [Linux Rekoobe Operating with New, Undetected Malware Samples](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2020/01/linux-rekoobe-operating-with-new-undetected-malware-samples/): New statically compiled variants of Rekoobe, a Linux trojan first reported in 2015, evade detection after its authors stripped attributive strings. (2020-01-20)
- [ChinaZ Updates Toolkit by Introducing New, Undetected Malware](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/12/chinaz-updates-toolkit-by-introducing-new-undetected-malware/): ChinaZ is using new low-detection Linux malware, NewManager, AmpManager and DDoSManager, which combine backdoor and DDoS bot capabilities. (2019-12-13)
- [ACBackdoor: Analysis of a New Multiplatform Backdoor](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/11/acbackdoor-analysis-of-a-new-multiplatform-backdoor/): ACBackdoor is an undocumented backdoor with Linux and Windows variants sharing one C2 protocol; the Windows variant was delivered via Fallout Exploit Kit. (2019-11-18)
- [PureLocker: New Ransomware-as-a-Service Being Used in Targeted Attacks Against Servers](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/11/purelocker-ransomware-being-used-in-targeted-attacks-against-servers/): PureLocker, ransomware written in PureBasic and used in targeted attacks on servers, shares code with the more_eggs backdoor sold by a MaaS provider. (2019-11-12)
- [Mapping the Connections Inside Russia’s APT Ecosystem](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/09/russian-apt-ecosystem/): Joint research with Check Point mapping thousands of Russian APT samples finds actors rarely share code, which may point to a focus on operational security. (2019-09-24)
- [Russian Cybercrime Group FullofDeep Behind QNAPCrypt Ransomware Campaigns](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/09/russian-cybercrime-group-fullofdeep-behind-qnapcrypt-ransomware-campaigns/): A new QNAPCrypt sample shares code and encryption with the 15 campaigns we halted in July. Its ransom note and strings point to Russian group FullofDeep. (2019-09-20)
- [MoP – "Master of Puppets" – Advanced malware tracking framework revealed at BlackHat Arsenal 2019](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/08/mop-master-of-puppets-advanced-malware-tracking-framework-revealed-at-blackhat-arsenal-2019/): MoP (Master of Puppets) is an open-source Python framework for building malware trackers that simulate infected workstations to interact with C2 servers. (2019-08-14)
- [Watching the WatchBog: New BlueKeep Scanner and Linux Exploits](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/07/watching-the-watchbog-new-bluekeep-scanner-and-linux-exploits/): A new WatchBog cryptomining botnet version hit an estimated 4,500 Linux machines, adding fresh Jira, Exim and Solr exploits and a BlueKeep RDP scanner. (2019-07-24)
- [EvilGnome: Rare Malware Spying on Linux Desktop Users](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/07/evilgnome-rare-malware-spying-on-linux-desktop-users/): EvilGnome is an undetected Linux backdoor posing as a Gnome shell extension that takes screenshots, records audio and steals files. Linked to Gamaredon Group. (2019-07-17)
- [How We Seized 15 Active Ransomware Campaigns Targeting Linux File Storage Servers](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/07/seizing-15-active-ransomware-campaigns-targeting-linux-file-storage-servers/): We simulated over 1,091 infections to exhaust QNAPCrypt’s static Bitcoin wallet list, temporarily halting 15 ransomware campaigns targeting QNAP NAS servers. (2019-07-10)
- [HiddenWasp Malware Stings Targeted Linux Systems](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/05/hiddenwasp-malware-targeting-linux-systems/): HiddenWasp is a Linux trojan with a rootkit, undetected at discovery, used for targeted remote control and reusing code from Mirai and the Azazel rootkit. (2019-05-29)
- [Technical Analysis: Pacha Group Competing against Rocke Group for Cryptocurrency Mining Foothold on the Cloud](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/05/technical-analysis-cryptocurrency-mining-war-on-the-cloud/): New Linux.GreedyAntd variants show Pacha Group targeting cloud environments and using blacklists to remove Rocke Group miners and cloud security agents. (2019-05-09)
- [Technical Analysis: Pacha Group Deploying Undetected Cryptojacking Campaigns on Linux Servers](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/02/technical-analysis-pacha-group/): Pacha Group, likely of Chinese origin, runs undetected Linux.GreedyAntd cryptojacking campaigns whose IPC-linked multi-stage design evades dynamic analysis. (2019-02-28)
- [ChinaZ Revelations: Revealing ChinaZ Relationships with other Chinese Threat Actor Groups](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2019/01/chinaz-relations/): We tracked the ChinaZ DDoS group through honeypot hits and its file servers, and found possible connections to Nitol, MrBlack and ServStart actors. (2019-01-07)
- [Muhstik Botnet Reloaded: New Variants Targeting phpMyAdmin Servers](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2018/11/muhstik-botnet-reloaded-new-variants-targeting-phpmyadmin-servers/): New Muhstik botnet variants add a scanner module targeting phpMyAdmin web servers, with code likely borrowed and modified from the open-source Pnscan tool. (2018-11-12)
- [Paleontology: The Unknown Origins of Lazarus Malware](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2018/10/paleontology-the-unknown-origins-of-lazarus-malware/): Lazarus malware appears to be built on CasperPhpTrojan, an open-source RAT from a Chinese code site, found via a low-detection sample we call CasperTroy. (2018-10-31)
- [APT37: Final1stspy Reaping the FreeMilk](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2018/10/apt37-final1stspy-reaping-the-freemilk/): An earlier Final1stspy DLL shares unique code with ROKRAT from the FreeMilk campaign, adding evidence that links NOKKI and Final1stspy to APT37 (Group123). (2018-10-03)
- [Prince of Persia: The Sands of Foudre](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2018/08/prince-of-persia-the-sands-of-foudre/): Foudre version 8 shows the Prince of Persia (Infy) campaign, believed to be Iranian, is still active, using a protest video as a lure and an updated DGA. (2018-08-17)
- [Examining Code Reuse Reveals Undiscovered Links Among North Korea’s Malware Families](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2018/08/examining-code-reuse-reveals-undiscovered-links-among-north-koreas-malware-families/): Joint research with McAfee maps code reuse across malware attributed to North Korea, from 2009 attacks to WannaCry, revealing links between groups and families. (2018-08-06)
- [Building Your Bullet Proof Incident Response Plan](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2018/03/building-your-bullet-proof-incident-response-plan/): An incident response plan depends on finding real malware among false positives. Code reuse detection helps SOC teams classify threats and remediate sooner. (2018-03-15)
- [Yet Another Distraction? A New Version of North Korean Ransomware Hermes Has Emerged](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2018/02/another-distraction-new-version-north-korean-ransomware-hermes/): Hermes 2.1 ransomware shares code with the Hermes version used as a diversion in a Taiwan bank heist and thought to originate from North Korea’s Lazarus group. (2018-02-08)
- [BLOCKBUSTED: Lazarus, Blockbuster, and North Korea](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2017/12/blockbusted-lazarus-blockbuster-north-korea/): Code overlaps in Lazarus samples from 2014 to 2017, including shared C&C command handlers, link Blockbuster campaign malware to other North Korean attacks. (2017-12-12)
- [Don’t Be Fooled By Malware Signed with Stolen Certificates](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2017/12/dont-fooled-malware-signed-stolen-certificates-intezer-analyze-detects-major-breaches-security/): Malware signed with stolen certificates, like Stuxnet and the CCleaner backdoor, bypasses tools that trust signatures. Code reuse analysis checks code instead. (2017-12-07)
- [IcedID Banking Trojan Shares Code with Pony 2.0 Trojan](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2017/11/icedid-banking-trojan-shares-code-pony-2-0-trojan/): The IcedID banking trojan payload reuses code from Pony 2.0, mostly functions for stealing email credentials such as Outlook’s GrabOutlook routine. (2017-11-13)
- [Silence of the Moles](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2017/11/silenceofthemoles/): The loader of Silence, malware aimed at financial institutions, shares unique code with the Mole ransomware loader, a possible sign of the same threat actor. (2017-11-01)
- [NotPetya Returns as Bad Rabbit](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2017/10/notpetya-returns-bad-rabbit/): Bad Rabbit ransomware reuses NotPetya code: 27% of its fake Adobe Flash installer loader and 13% of its encryption module match NotPetya samples. (2017-10-25)
- [Evidence Aurora Operation Still Active Part 2: More Ties Uncovered Between CCleaner Hack & Chinese Hackers](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2017/10/evidence-aurora-operation-still-active-part-2-more-ties-uncovered-between-ccleaner-hack-chinese-hackers/): Code shared by the CCleaner stage 2 payload and APT17 samples strengthens the link to the Axiom group, in an attack we assess was most likely state-sponsored. (2017-10-02)
- [Evidence Aurora Operation Still Active: Supply Chain Attack Through CCleaner](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2017/09/evidence-aurora-operation-still-active-supply-chain-attack-through-ccleaner/): A unique base64 function shared by the CCleaner 5.33 backdoor and earlier APT17 samples suggests the Operation Aurora group was still active in 2017. (2017-09-20)
- [New Variants of Agent.BTZ/ComRAT Found: The Threat That Hit The Pentagon In 2008 Still Evolving; Part 2/2](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2017/09/new-variants-of-agent-btz-comrat-found-part-2/): How we hunted new Agent.BTZ/ComRAT variants: filtering out library code, isolating unique functions kept since 2007 and turning them into YARA rules. (2017-09-13)
- [New Variants of Agent.BTZ/ComRAT Found: The Threat That Hit The Pentagon In 2008 Still Evolving; Part 1/2](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2017/08/new-variants-of-agent-btz-comrat-found/): New Agent.BTZ/ComRAT variants from the Turla group: about a dozen new samples and over 70 unknown IPs and domains abusing satellite internet providers. (2017-08-07)
- ["EternalMiner" Copycats exploiting SambaCry for cryptocurrency mining](https://research.intezer.com/blog/2017/07/eternalminer-copycats/): CopyMiner: copycats exploiting the SambaCry Samba vulnerability to install a cryptominer and the Tsunami backdoor, with daily updates from backup servers. (2017-07-26)

## Knowledge Base

- [Beginner's guide to malware analysis and reverse engineering](https://research.intezer.com/docs/reverse-engineering/): A beginner’s guide to malware analysis: setting the analysis goal, then initial triage of file format, known threats, packing, strings and the import table.


### Malware Reverse Engineering for Beginners

Reverse engineering basics for malware analysts with no RE experience: assembly, the CPU and stack, disassemblers, and how malware is packed and delivered.

- [Malware Reverse Engineering for Beginners](https://research.intezer.com/docs/malware_re_101/): overview of this guide
- [From 0x0](https://research.intezer.com/docs/malware_re_101/part1/): An introduction to malware reverse engineering: when to reverse a sample, how the CPU, registers and stack work, assembly instructions and disassemblers.
- [Packers, crypters, protectors, loaders...](https://research.intezer.com/docs/malware_re_101/part2/): Packers, crypters, protectors and loaders explained, how to detect packed malware statically and dynamically, and unpacking examples with UPX and Locky.

### How to Analyze

How to analyze the file types attackers use to deliver malware: LNK shortcuts, Office documents, PDFs, phishing emails and MSI installers, with free tools.

- [How to Analyze](https://research.intezer.com/docs/how-to-analyze/): overview of this guide
- [LNK Files](https://research.intezer.com/docs/how-to-analyze/lnk/): How threat actors abuse Windows LNK shortcut files, how the Shell Link Binary format works, and how to analyze and detect malicious LNK files with LnkParse3.
- [Microsoft Office Files](https://research.intezer.com/docs/how-to-analyze/office/): How malicious Office files deliver malware through OLE, OOXML and RTF: macros, DDE abuse, template injection and known vulnerabilities, and how to analyze each.
- [PDF Files](https://research.intezer.com/docs/how-to-analyze/pdf/): How the PDF file format is abused to deliver malware, and how to investigate suspicious PDFs with free tools such as peepdf, with two malicious examples.
- [Phishing Emails](https://research.intezer.com/docs/how-to-analyze/phishing/): How to inspect phishing email files: sender addresses, headers, attachments and links, plus a real campaign that used a short URL and a packed payload.
- [MSI Installer Files](https://research.intezer.com/docs/how-to-analyze/msi/): How attackers abuse MSI installers and custom actions, how the MSI database is structured, and a hands-on malicious MSI analysis with msitools and msidiff.

### Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) files

The Linux ELF executable format from the ground up: sections and segments, symbols, relocations and dynamic linking, and how malware authors abuse them.

- [Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) files](https://research.intezer.com/docs/elf/): overview of this guide
- [Sections and Segments](https://research.intezer.com/docs/elf/part1/): How an ELF file is laid out: the ELF header, the section header table, the program header table, and how sections map into segments loaded into memory.
- [Symbols](https://research.intezer.com/docs/elf/part2/): What symbolic information is in ELF files, the ELF symbol structure, and how the .symtab and .dynsym symbol tables relate to their string tables.
- [Relocations](https://research.intezer.com/docs/elf/part3/): How ELF relocations connect symbolic references to their definitions, the structure of relocation entries, and the x86 and x86_64 relocation types.
- [Dynamic Linking](https://research.intezer.com/docs/elf/part4/): How dynamic linking works in ELF files: static versus dynamic linking, what the dynamic linker does at load time, and lazy linking through the PLT and GOT.

### ELF Malware Analysis 101

A training track for Linux malware: the ELF threat landscape, then static and dynamic analysis of real ELF samples with tools you can run on a Linux VM.

- [ELF Malware Analysis 101](https://research.intezer.com/docs/elf-malware/): overview of this guide
- [Linux Threats No Longer an Afterthought](https://research.intezer.com/docs/elf-malware/part1/): The Linux threat landscape, how ELF malware infects systems, and why antivirus detection of ELF files is unreliable, illustrated with VirusTotal results.
- [Initial Analysis](https://research.intezer.com/docs/elf-malware/part2/): Static analysis of ELF malware: symbols, segments, sections, the ELF header and strings, code reuse, and detecting UPX, custom UPX and VMprotect packers.
- [Advanced Analysis](https://research.intezer.com/docs/elf-malware/part3/): Dynamic analysis of ELF malware: preparing a VM, the proc filesystem, tracing syscalls, finding persistence, sniffing traffic, and a Rekoobe sample walkthrough.

### .NET Malware 101

How .NET malware is compiled and run by the CLR, and how to navigate a .NET assembly’s metadata, tokens and method bodies with dnSpy, ILSpy and PEStudio.

- [.NET Malware 101](https://research.intezer.com/docs/dotnet/): overview of this guide
- [Analyzing the .NET Executable File Structure](https://research.intezer.com/docs/dotnet/exe-structure/): Inside the .NET executable format: CLR compilation and runtime, metadata streams and tables, tokens, the manifest and method bodies, using the Sunburst sample.

### Memory Analysis 101

Memory forensics for fileless malware and injected code: what a memory image reveals, why manual analysis is hard, and the tools that make it practical.

- [Memory Analysis 101](https://research.intezer.com/docs/memory/): overview of this guide
- [Understanding Memory Threats and Forensic Tools](https://research.intezer.com/docs/memory/tools/): Memory forensics for in-memory threats: what it recovers, why manual analysis is hard, and finding a Cobalt Strike beacon with WinPmem, Volatility and YARA.

### URL Analysis 101

How phishing URLs are manipulated to look trustworthy, from cybersquatting to short URLs, and how to detect them at scale with machine learning.

- [URL Analysis 101](https://research.intezer.com/docs/url-analysis/): overview of this guide
- [A Beginner's Guide to Phishing URLs](https://research.intezer.com/docs/url-analysis/part1/): The anatomy of a URL and the tricks phishing links use: subdomain, TLD and typo cybersquatting, special characters, short URLs and HTML concealment.
- [Automating Phishing Investigations with Machine Learning](https://research.intezer.com/docs/url-analysis/part2/): List-based versus machine learning detection of phishing URLs, the trade-offs of each, and extracting URL features to classify phishing links with an SVM.
